 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 28.05.2021 at about 5.45 p.m., the Petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-HM-7159 on Bennergatta Road and when he reached near Koli Farm Junction, Gottigere, at that time, the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-A-0089 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and run over the motorcycle.
Consequently, the petitioner sustained grievous/crush injuries.
The Motorcycle was also damaged.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Vijayashree Hospital and given first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein he had taken treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery.
He has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards treatment, medicine, conveyance and nourishment, hospital charges and incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a Books Delivery boy at M/s Byjus, deputed by M/s Golden Star, Bengaluru and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the Owner and respondent No.2 is Insurer of Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-M-0089 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence,
this Petition.
Ajith.

2 5.
In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed objections to the main petition.
Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus.

Further he contended that the accident took place due to negligence of the injured himself, if he had taken little care while riding the vehicle in the said road, the said accident would have been avoided.
He further contended that the driver of the bus was having valid driving licence to drive the bus at the time of said accident.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus.
It admitted the policy.

Further it contended that, the Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-0089 was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and the police to get the compensation by this respondent.

Further it contended that the driver of said bus was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident and also bus was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

Further it contended that the jurisdictional police after thorough investigation have filed a charge sheet U/Sec.66(1) R/W Sec.192(A) of the MV Act, stating that the bus was not having valid Permit and FC as on the date of the accident.
Further it contended that petition is bad for Non joinder of necessary party such as the owner and insurer of the TP motorcycle and driver of our bus are necessary parties to the proceedings.
Further it contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident, hence the petitioner has violated Sec. 129 of MV Act.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 28.05.2021 at about 5.45 p.m. at Koli Farm Gate junction, B.G.Road, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Bus bearing No.KA-51-A-0089?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.18.
Thereafter, the petitioner got examined PW.2 and got marked three documents as per Ex.P.19 to 21 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.2 examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
Respondent No.1 has not chosen to lead evidence.

Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 9.

Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 28.05.2021 at about 5.45 p.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51-A-0089 by its driver.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51-A-0089 by its driver.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-18.
He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 is the true copy of FIR along with complaint, Ex.P.2 is the true copy of spot panchanama along with sketch map, Ex.P.3 is the true copy of Notice u/s133 of MV Act, Ex.P.4 is the true copy of reply notice, Ex.P.5 is the true copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the true copy of Charge sheet, Ex.P.7 is the true copy of Wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.9 is the Medical bills,
Ex.P.10 is the photographs, Ex.P.11 is the CD, Ex.P.12 to 14 are the notarized copy of PAN card,

Ltd., Ex.P.16 is the Original ID Card of PW.1, Ex.P.17 is the Bank statement, Ex.P.18 is the X-rays,
Ex.P.19 is the Clinical notes, Ex.P.20 Case sheet and Ex.P.21 is the X-ray.
12.

Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR with Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Hulimavu Traffic Police Station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the driver of Private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51-A- 0089 for the offences punishable under Sec.279,
337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the spot panchanama with sketch which shows that it was made in the presence of panchas.
They show that the accident place was a junction.
They further show that both vehicle were proceeding on the same direction simultaneously, the driver of the offending bus took sudden right turn and dashed against the bike of petitioner.
Ex.P.3 and 4 are the Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act to the owner of the offending vehicle and Reply given by owner (Respondent No.1) of the offending vehicle.
Wherein, the Respondent No.1 admitted that at the time of accident, one Syed Sunnu S/o Syed Sharif who is the accused in the charge sheet was driving the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV report which shows that accident did not cause due to any mechanical defects.
It further shows that bus got scratched on front right side bumper and bike got damaged to its head light, rest foot crash guard and silencer.
It justify the fact of involvement of vehicle in question and the nature of accident as narrated by the petitioner.

The Ex.P.6 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the Hulimavu Traffic Police have Charge-sheeted the driver of the Private bus bearing Ajith.S vs Gopi.S.N on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24955146/
4 Reg. No.KA-51-A-0089 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and under Sec.66(1),
192(A) of IMV Act.
The Ex
. P.7 the Wound certificate which shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
13. PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.
During his cross examination, he has admitted that he was conscious after the accident.
Further admitted that the accident took place at Junction.
Further he admitted that the driver of the bus, took right turn at a speed of 20 k.m.
He denies the other suggestion of the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
Nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
14. The respondent No.2 has examined its Manager as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 i.e., true copy of policy.
He has deposed that he is not an eye witness.
He has not personally enquired about the accident with the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, he is hear say witness and his evidence would not be a deciding factor for negligence.
15. The charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Private bus bearing KA-51-A- 0089 and in the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
16. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Private bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-0089, Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 22 years.
He has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.13 to prove his age.
As per aadhar card his date of birth is shown as 25.04.1999.
The accident has taken place on 28.05.2021.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 22 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
18. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as Office boy and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

In this regard, he has produced a letter issued by Golden Star Facilities and Services Pvt. Ltd., and ID card at Ex.P.15 and 16 which shows that the petitioner was working as Office boy in the said organization and drawing salary of Rs.13,184/- p.m. and gross salary of Rs.14,791/-.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: But, the authority who issued the said letter has not been examined.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,000/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2021, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:

5 20.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. Degloving injury over right foot.
Wherein, the Doctor has opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injury sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
21. Bearing in mind the nature of the injury sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
22.

The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 29.05.2021 to 11.06.2021 at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bangalore.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He was underwent surgery.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.Chidanand K.J.C has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
The discharge summary marked at Ex.P.8 justifies the same.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 14 days.
23. Further, he might have taken at least two months for recovery.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head (@
Rs.15,000/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
24.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :

Ajith.S vs Gopi.S.N on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24955146/
6 25.
The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 11 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.9 amounting to Rs.73,221/-.
I have gone through the same.
There is no serious dispute about the medical bills.
Hence, the bills are accepted.
By rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.73,300/- as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

26. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he cannot continue his avocation, unable to use his right leg for nay purpose, unable to bear weight and unable to ride or drive any kind of vehicle.
27. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. Chidanand K.J.C as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, he got marked Clinical notes, Case sheet and X-ray at Ex.P.19 to 21.

He assessed permanent physical disability of whole body at 15%.
28.
In the cross-examination, PW.2 has admitted that the bones were united, but there is an infection and there is no loss of muscle Power.
He had taken oral opinion from the plastic surgeon.
He has seen the follow up records of injured.
According to the records, the injured has taken 4-5 times follow up treatment and no document has been produced before the court in this regard.
Further he admitted that all implants are removed.
29. The Doctor has assessed permanent disability of whole body at 15%.

Upon careful consideration of the assessment of disability made by PW.2 keeping in mind the fact that PW.1 personally appeared before this court and deposed, also keeping in mind the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 and the treatment which he has taken, Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed appears to be just and proper.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 15%
would be just and proper.
30. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.15,000/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 15%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.4,86,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 12 x 18 x15/100 =Rs.4,86,000/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,86,000/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:

1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-

diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 73,300/-

laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.4,86,000/-
Total Rs.6,62,300/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.6,62,300/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
32. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the bus bearing No.KA-51-A-0089.
There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

33. Now that this court has ascertained the compensation amount, the last aspect of the matter is regarding fixation of liability i.e., who should be made liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner?.
Precisely, it is the specific case of the respondent No.2 that there was no permit and FC as on the date of accident of the offending vehicle bus bearing registration No.KA-51-A-0089.

In this regard, Respondent No.2 has examined SDA of RTO as RW.1 and produced Ex.R.2 to R.4 i.e.,
authorisation letter given by the RTO, certificate of fitness and endorsement issued by the RTO.
As per Ex.R.3 FC of vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-0089 was valid from 08.12.2020 to 07.12.2021.
The accident has occurred on 28.05.2021.
Hence as on the date of accident the FC was valid.
As per Ex.R.4 endorsement issued by the RTO Electronic City Bengaluru no permit has been issued in respect of bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-0089.
He also produced the online copy of the Registeration details of the offending bus.

As per the said document, the offending bus had a permit from 19-05-2006 to 18.05.2016.
34.
Therefore it is crystal clear that the offending bus had no permit to ply on road at the time of accident.

The Respondent No.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle, except filling of written statement he has not contested the matter and not produced any evidence to prove that his bus had Ajith.S vs Gopi.S.N on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24955146/
8 permit to ply on road at the time of accident.
35. For the reasons discussed as supra, it is established that the offending bus bearing registration No. KA-51-A-0089 had no permit at the time of the accident.
36. The next aspect to be pondered upon now is, what is the effect, if offending vehicle had no permit to ply on road at the time of accident.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on the following citations:
1. (2018) 7 SCC 558 between Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Company Ltd., and others, Wherein hon'ble Apex court has held as under:
"24................. The principles laid down in Swaran Singh and Lakhmi Chand in that regard would not be applicable to the case at hand.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Company Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That apart, the insurer had taken the plea that the vehicle in question had no permit.
It does not require the wisdom of the 'Tripitaka' that the existence of a permit of any nature is a matter of documentary evidence.
Nothing has been brought on record by the insured to prove that he had a permit of the vehicle.
In such a situation, the onus cannot be cast on the insurer.

Therefore, the Tribunal as well as the High Court had directed that the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver.

entities.text: Rani and others Vs.National Insurance Co.Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accepting that defence, High Court absolving the insurer and fastening the liability on the insured i.e., the owner of offending vehicle directing him to satisfy the award - Held, even in such a case, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle - Order of High Court modified accordingly."

37. The essence of the said decisions is that even where the offending vehicle had no permit and the insurance company pleads that there is violation of policy conditions, if the vehicle had a valid and subsisting insurance policy, then the insurance company has to pay the compensation with liberty to recover the same from owner and rider.

Ajith.S vs Gopi.S.N on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24955146/
9 38.
The respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of policy in favor of respondent No.1 in respect of bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-A-0089.

Thereby fortifying the view taken by this Tribunal that the respondent No.2 should make good the compensation amount to the petitioner and then proceed against the respondent No.1 i.e., the owner to recover the same 39.

For the foregoing reasons this court finds no hesitation in holding that the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with liberty to recover the same from respondent No.1.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the partly affirmative.
40. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.6,62,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.

The Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is held liable to pay the compensation;
The Respondent No.2 insurance company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest (supra) within 60 days from the date of the Award and recover it from the Respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle as per law.
After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.1, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic accident.
Consequently, the petitioner sustained grievous/crush injuries.
The Motorcycle was also damaged.
